Benna Bok

By: Eugene Botha | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
... beware this online store.

Unique Selling Point:
Online commerce is growing rapidly, but there are lots of scammers. This is just one example.

Summary:
Benna Bok sells luxury shoes and handbag online, but clients either do not receive goods or receive inferior/faulty goods. The vast majority of clients do not receive anything and when asking for refunds they get blocked on social media and the website. A few who have used attorneys or threats, sometimes do receive refunds. This is a good example of how online business can go wrong.

Further information:
Benna Bok sells luxury shoes and handbag online, but clients either do not receive goods or receive inferior/faulty goods. The vast majority of clients do not receive anything and when asking for refunds they get blocked on social media and the website. A few who have used attorneys or threats, sometimes do receive refunds. This is a good example of how online business can go wrong.

We have had in excess of 30 complaints at Carte Blanche and when we followed up, we found a Facebook group online called Benna Bok Refund, with in excess of 100 people -- all being scammed and out of pocket and being blocked by the people behind Benna Bok. This group of people have now approached an attorney for a class action against Benna Bok and to lay criminal charges.

The people behind Benna Bok has had numerous online businesses, doing exactly the same -- advertising, having an online store with customers not receiving anything. Then they shut the store down, and start a new one. The previous stores were: Franella, Karoo Ella, Nelle Designer Hats, Bella Bok, Luna Cherry and Pure Clothing. They are a couple from Pretoria: Frank and Petro Vermeulen Botha of Montana.

They actually have a small factory on the premises where they live but our information is that the last month or so the only bought two sheets of leather -- not nearly enough to fill all the orders. They currently have a sale and it seems they are on a drive to get as much as possible and leave the country.

They threaten everybody who asks questions and people tend to back down then. At the beginning of October and two days ago they posted apologies and promises and nothing comes of it. People are still not getting refunds and goods.

They have gone through several sets of attorneys, who in the end do not want to provide them with services.

They also say a buy called Frank Vermeulen caused their business damage (coincidence: "Frank Vermeulen" is a combination of Frank's frist name and Petro's mainden name). They claim to have an interdict against him - we will check it out. They also claim a disgruntled customer attacked their factory, and that caused delays. We will also check that out.

We have the following:

Edith Barnard -- founder of the group Benna Bok Refund who has organized a group of disgruntled customers.

Nikola -- a niece of Hester who worked for them and have inside information about their operations and the scamming. She is willing to speak, if she can remain anonymous.

Shalini Chetty from Pretoria who also wrote to us and who is still waiting for an order or refund since the end of August.

Diederick Stopforth of Sedgefield. He threatened them with Carte Blanche and got a refund.

We have about 30 other case studies waiting for refunds, and a list of more than 100 people on the Benna Bok Refund site.

Gideon Pienaar, the attorney who taking on the class action and he is willing to speak about the case and also give advice to consumers.

Modus operandi:

Gather as much info as possible

Film Frank and Petro at their house and factory

Try to get into factory to see what is actually happening there and if anything is being manufactured

Call the Bothas for an interview

If not willing, door-stop them





Extra Budget Items:
Interview in Sedgefield

Case Study:
Edith Barnard
Shalini Chetty
Diederick Stopforth
Petro Botha

Expert:
Mr. Gideon Pienaar

Hidden Camera: No

Legal: Yes
Reason for legal: Complex legal issues in scam

Press Release:


Online commerce is expanding rapidly. But what recourse do customers have when things go wrong, and returns and refunds don’t materialize? One local online store that sells luxury handbags and shoes has incurred the wrath of hundreds of clients who either received nothing or were sent inferior and faulty goods after they paid for the beautiful items on screen. Carte Blanche confronts the owners of the business.

Script:


LINK 1:
….. and buy!

More and more of us are doing it nowadays. Online shopping. It is convenient, fast and good value for money! But it is not always smooth sailing.

V/O:
That is exactly what this group of women found out. Before today they did not know each other at all. But they all have one thing in common – they have done online shopping that went pear-shaped. They all feel that they have been conned by the same on-line shop.

Victims:
I am Shalini Chetty and I have been scammed by Benna Bok
I am Lynette and I have been scammed by Benna Bok
I’m Estelle and I was scammed by Benna Bok
Hi, I’m Yvetter and I have been scammed by Benna Bok
I am Erna and I was scammed by Benna Bok

V/O:
Benna Bok is an online shopping portal selling luxury leather items online. And their website in impressive and the goods are definitely desirable. And the pricing is really attractive, with many specials. This is what is currently on their website.

However, literally dozens of disgruntled customers have contacted Carte Blanche about Benna Bok the last few months.

LINK 2:
Upon further investigation we found many serious complaints on Hello Peter, and we found that there is a Facebook Group called Benna Bok Refunds and a Whatsapp Group specifically for Benna Bok customers.

V/O:
In fact, there are 465 members on the Benna Bok Refund group and 197 members on the Whatsapp group. Edith Barnard started the WhatsApp group. She ordered a handbag and shoes, but never received it. She struggled to find out what was going on.

Edith:
Eventually we got the telephone numbers for Petro and Frank Botha, the owners, and we WhatsApp them, but as soon as you ask questions, they’re just ugly, they cut you off and block you.

Devi:
So what would they say on WhatsApp or One Messenger?

Edith:
Umm, your order is on its way, your order is in processing, your order is in packaging, and once you ask for a refund they become ugly, they say speak to my lawyer.

Devi:
When did you realize you were not the only one?

Edith:
Once they blocked me I started Googling and going onto Facebook and came upon the refund page.

V/O:
The Benna Bok Refund page had countless complaints similar to Edith’s: poor service, no deliveries, no communication, false promises of refunds and hundreds of people out of pocket for thousands of rand. Edith started her group to see if they could mobilise against Benna Bok as a group. All these women feel strongly that they have been scammed and deliberately lied to. And it seems that that impression is not far off the mark.

LINK 3:
We managed to trace two former employees who worked at the company and who can provide some insight into the operations at Benna Bok headquarters.

V/O:
Lorraine de Kock was employed to handle customer queries and told to stall customers.

Devi:
What were people complaining about?

Lorraine:
Die meeste is … toe ek nou daar is … het daar mense gekom van Mei-Junie- Julie wat al kla my pakkie is nog nie afgelewer nie. En dan sê ek “Ek sien hier op die sisteem die ding is nog op die peoduction line, laat ek net verder vir jou kyk. Dis omtrent die tipe van ding wat jy moet sê.

Devi:
Was any of that true?

Lorraine:
Nee, dit was nie waar nie. Dit was ‘n rympie wat jy moes opsê.

V/O:
Trudie, who wants to remain anonymous, also worked at Benna Bok.

Trudie:
They told me you have to lie to the clients. Tell them it is in processing, and we will buy leather. And I go “When are you going to buy the leather?” “We’ll go Friday.” But there is no leather and it is Monday. And then, when I started to ask too much questions for the clients, thye just told me “no, you are going to do the Facebook thing. But here is a copy paste. You do not respond on you own. You only give them this.

Devi:
But all lies?

Trudie:
This is everything they told me to say.

Devi
But Lies?

Trudie
Lies,Yes.

V/O:
We visited the offices of Benna Bok and Per thru Botha, the only director of the company admitted that before she started Benna Bok, she had two other online stores called Franella and Karoo Ella. Both these stores ran into trouble with irate clients and were closed last year.

She also showed us the room on the premises where goods were being manufactured.

Devi:
So let’s move on a little bit then. Let’s talk specifically now about Benna Bok. So, people are claiming that they don’t get their orders.

Petro:
Yes.

Devi:
So, why aren’t people getting their orders?

Petro:
That is a very good question and that is a very big thing. There is not only just one reason. At the end of July my grandmother passed away and I closed my business fortwo weeks. After that we had a big boom in business and we got behind on orders. I bought 3 extra machines and employed six people to try and get the orders out as quick as possible and to try and catch up.

Devi:
So the allegation is that people were told to stall consumers over a eriod of time and tell them it was going through this process and then it was going to packaging and yet there was no stock and nothing was actually happening. Do you deny that?

Petro:
The ladies who worked for me did not know what to tell customers anymore, because I told them this od what we are telling customers. So, when someone phones and she is screaming at you, they say it is at quality control. I didn’t tell her to tell that. That is what she is doing because she is panicking because the customer phoned her. So, we had a problem with customer care.

Devi:
But those were lies?

Petro:
Those were lies! I did not tell them to tell it.

V/O:
The irate customers found out where they lived and started to vandalize their property . In addition, Benna Bok was being slammed on a variety of platforms on the internet which Petro claims damaged their business. She says a fake Facebook page began posting negative stuff about them from August, and they actually started to receive death threats.

Devi:
So the same story…..

Petro:
The same story, we get called the “scam couple” and all kinds of things.

You don’t think you deserve that title?

Petro:
No

Devi:
And you don’t think that people are calling you a scamster because they are paying for products that thye are not getting.

Petro:
I can understand that. But I did not tale people’s money and ran away. I have a business that I am trying to run.

Devi:
But yes, as we sit right now. How many people still don’t have their goods?

Petro:
I am not sure. We are working on it.

Devi:
That is not good enough.

Petro:
Yesterday we sent out 11 parcels.

V/O:
Petro then showed us 11 recent courier waybills. And they continue to advertise special promotions on their website.

Devi:
If you could not manage the orders, why are you having flash sales, Black Friday sales

Petro:
To keep the cash flow going.

Devi:
For you!

Petro:
J.. No for the business.

Devi:
Which is you? Yes.

Petro:
But the business is not only me. It is the fifteen households that I feed.

V/O:
At some stage Petro did indeed have 15 employees, but only two remain.

Devi:
You are using other people’s money to roll your business.

Petro:
Roll my business? Meaning?

Taking other people’s money so you can carry on.

Petro:
Why don’t they give me a chance to put down my phone and to work and to get things out.

Why do you want them to give you a chance? They gave you their money, they want the goods.


Petro:
So what am I supposed to do, Devi.

I don’t know what you are supposed to do. I am just saying: “don’t run a business if you can’t provide the goods”. That’s what I am saying.

Petro:
I refunded R350 000.I sold my husband’s car to refund people. That’s what I did to try and save my business.

But you know you are breaking the law.

Petro:
Devi, I am trying my best.

Ja, but you are breaking the law.

Petro:
What am I supposed to do? Do you think it is fair that people call me a scam?

Well, they paid for goods that they haven’t received for months.

Petro:
OK. But do you think if I am still delivering, that I am a scam?

But you are not delivering to everybody that you owe. A large number of people are going to say that you are a scam because do you know what is the test for this? Did they pay you for the goods? Yes. Did you give them what they paid for?

Petro:
Not all of them no.

That’s the answer. You can’t run a business like that because people will then claim it is stealing.

Petro:
I don’t know what to do anymore. I mean, I am not sleeping. And I don’t know what to do. I am trying my best, but it is not good enough.

V/O:
Attorney Gideon Pienaar has been retained by the WhatsApp group to help them get justice as a group because it is not really feasible for individuals to go to court over small amounts of money.

Gideon
The legal system in South Africa is very good, but it is slow, and obviously, costly. So it is not possible to recover monies. They knew that if they did not perform in terms of their website, that they would not, that these creditors would not be able to individually go after them and instruct lawyers left right and centre. So that is why we started this class action.

Devi:
So what is the plan moving forward?

Gideon:
Well, there is only one real document that will tell you what happened here. The bank statements. The bank statements of all these businesses will tell the story whether these people really had the intent to either perform or refund their creditors. And the only way that you can deal with it is either do the criminal prosecution, lay criminal charges or obviously a liquidation. Liquidate the company because the company is not in a position to pay its creditors, and from there you can have inquires and also get the bank statements.

LINK 5:
Attorney Pienaar has kept his word and has since we interviewed him, laid a criminal charge against Benna Bok at Sinoville Police Station.

V/O:
And it is exactly this kind of action Edith had in mind when she started the Whatsapp group.

Edith:
Two hundred very upset girls who are minus their shoes and minus their handbags. That is just asking for trouble. Yes.

And they continue to advertise special promotions on their website. Devi: If you could not manage the orders, why are you having flash sales, Black Friday sales Petro: To keep the cash flow going. Devi: For you! Petro: J.. No for the business. Devi: Which is you? Yes. Petro: But the business is not only me. It is the fifteen households that I feed. V/O: At some stage Petro did indeed have 15 employees, but only two remain. Devi: You are using other people’s money to roll your business. Petro: Roll my business? Meaning? Taking other people’s money so you can carry on. Petro: Why don’t they give me a chance to put down my phone and to work and to get things out. Why do you want them to give you a chance? They gave you their money, they want the goods. Petro: So what am I supposed to do, Devi. I don’t know what you are supposed to do. I am just saying: “don’t run a business if you can’t provide the goods”. That’s what I am saying. Petro: I refunded R350 000.I sold my husband’s car to refund people. That’s what I did to try and save my business. But you know you are breaking the law. Petro: Devi, I am trying my best. Ja, but you are breaking the law. Petro: What am I supposed to do? Do you think it is fair that people call me a scam? Well, they paid for goods that they haven’t received for months. Petro: OK. But do you think if I am still delivering, that I am a scam? But you are not delivering to everybody that you owe. A large number of people are going to say that you are a scam because do you know what is the test for this? Did they pay you for the goods? Yes. Did you give them what they paid for? Petro: Not all of them no. That’s the answer. You can’t run a business like that because people will then claim it is stealing. Petro: I don’t know what to do anymore. I mean, I am not sleeping. And I don’t know what to do. I am trying my best, but it is not good enough. V/O: Attorney Gideon Pienaar has been retained by the WhatsApp group to help them get justice as a group because it is not really feasible for individuals to go to court over small amounts of money. Gideon The legal system in South Africa is very good, but it is slow, and obviously, costly. So it is not possible to recover monies. They knew that if they did not perform in terms of their website, that they would not, that these creditors would not be able to individually go after them and instruct lawyers left right and centre. So that is why we started this class action. Devi: So what is the plan moving forward? Gideon: Well, there is only one real document that will tell you what happened here. The bank statements. The bank statements of all these businesses will tell the story whether these people really had the intent to either perform or refund their creditors. And the only way that you can deal with it is either do the criminal prosecution, lay criminal charges or obviously a liquidation. Liquidate the company because the company is not in a position to pay its creditors, and from there you can have inquires and also get the bank statements. LINK 5: Attorney Pienaar has kept his word and has since we interviewed him, laid a criminal charge against Benna Bok at Sinoville Police Station. V/O: And it is exactly this kind of action Edith had in mind when she started the Whatsapp group. Edith: Two hundred very upset girls who are minus their shoes and minus their handbags. That is just asking for trouble. Yes.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Online commerce is growing rapidly, but there are lots of scammers. This is just one example.
metadata.Summary: Benna Bok sells luxury shoes and handbag online, but clients either do not receive goods or receive inferior/faulty goods. The vast majority of clients do not receive anything and when asking for refunds they get blocked on social media and the website. A few who have used attorneys or threats, sometimes do receive refunds. This is a good example of how online business can go wrong.
metadata.Further information: Benna Bok sells luxury shoes and handbag online, but clients either do not receive goods or receive inferior/faulty goods. The vast majority of clients do not receive anything and when asking for refunds they get blocked on social media and the website. A few who have used attorneys or threats, sometimes do receive refunds. This is a good example of how online business can go wrong. We have had in excess of 30 complaints at Carte Blanche and when we followed up, we found a Facebook group online called Benna Bok Refund, with in excess of 100 people -- all being scammed and out of pocket and being blocked by the people behind Benna Bok. This group of people have now approached an attorney for a class action against Benna Bok and to lay criminal charges. The people behind Benna Bok has had numerous online businesses, doing exactly the same -- advertising, having an online store with customers not receiving anything. Then they shut the store down, and start a new one. The previous stores were: Franella, Karoo Ella, Nelle Designer Hats, Bella Bok, Luna Cherry and Pure Clothing. They are a couple from Pretoria: Frank and Petro Vermeulen Botha of Montana. They actually have a small factory on the premises where they live but our information is that the last month or so the only bought two sheets of leather -- not nearly enough to fill all the orders. They currently have a sale and it seems they are on a drive to get as much as possible and leave the country. They threaten everybody who asks questions and people tend to back down then. At the beginning of October and two days ago they posted apologies and promises and nothing comes of it. People are still not getting refunds and goods. They have gone through several sets of attorneys, who in the end do not want to provide them with services. They also say a buy called Frank Vermeulen caused their business damage (coincidence: "Frank Vermeulen" is a combination of Frank's frist name and Petro's mainden name). They claim to have an interdict against him - we will check it out. They also claim a disgruntled customer attacked their factory, and that caused delays. We will also check that out. We have the following: Edith Barnard -- founder of the group Benna Bok Refund who has organized a group of disgruntled customers. Nikola -- a niece of Hester who worked for them and have inside information about their operations and the scamming. She is willing to speak, if she can remain anonymous. Shalini Chetty from Pretoria who also wrote to us and who is still waiting for an order or refund since the end of August. Diederick Stopforth of Sedgefield. He threatened them with Carte Blanche and got a refund. We have about 30 other case studies waiting for refunds, and a list of more than 100 people on the Benna Bok Refund site. Gideon Pienaar, the attorney who taking on the class action and he is willing to speak about the case and also give advice to consumers. Modus operandi: Gather as much info as possible Film Frank and Petro at their house and factory Try to get into factory to see what is actually happening there and if anything is being manufactured Call the Bothas for an interview If not willing, door-stop them
